title: Identity and composition for canonical derived étale cohomology pullback
statement: For schemes $X,Y,Z$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $f:Y\to X$ and $g:Z\to Y$. Let $K,L,N$ be bounded-below complexes of abelian etale sheaves on $X,Y,Z$, respectively [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $u:f^{-1}K\to L$ and $v:g^{-1}L\to N$ be complex morphisms [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Define $P_{f,u}^n:H^n(X,K)\to H^n(Y,L)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] as $H^n$ of the composite $R\Gamma_X(K)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_X(\eta_f)}R\Gamma_X Rf_* f^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\lambda_f}R\Gamma_Y(f^{-1}K)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma_Y(u)}R\Gamma_Y(L)$, where $\lambda_f$ is the canonical Leray comparison. Under the inverse-image identity and composition isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], $P_{\mathrm{id}_X,e_K}^n=\mathrm{id}$ and $P_{f\circ g,\,v\circ g^{-1}(u)\circ c^{-1}}^n=P_{g,v}^n\circ P_{f,u}^n$ for every integer $n$.

proof.text: For the identity clause, rewrite P using hP. The private idFactors calculation identifies the localized identity comparison with the exact-functor factorization followed by Q of the complex identity map. The mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac equation then identifies the entire complex-to-derived map with the localization of upperStarId. Apply the derived unit-Leray identity and then homology, which preserves identity. All localization glue is proved explicitly in Lean.

For composition, rewrite all three occurrences of P using hP. The private compFactors lemma combines mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac to identify the complex comparison for g≫f. Naturality of the factorization moves Q(v) past the second factorization. The private unitLeray_naturality lemma is naturality of the whiskered adjunction unit followed by the whiskered Leray comparison. Use it to move the first lifted complex morphism past the second unit-Leray composite. Combine with the derived unit-Leray composition equation and apply homology preservation of composition. These are the explicit hf, hv, hn, hh calculations in the Lean proof.
